director.chapterArc: A tactical realization of light as a barrier leads to an improvised defense that fails physically but succeeds tactically; allies arrive for combat, followed by a medical crisis where Jab's uncontrolled warmth saves Tonk at great personal cost. The scene shifts from high-stakes survival violence to exhausted dissociation and clinical triage.
director.restraintNote: Maintain the narrator as an observer of Jab's exhaustion rather than his panic. Let the combat feel clumsy and desperate, not choreographed. The healing moment must be read with physical weight and quiet inevitability, avoiding magical wonder. Keep Tonk's collapse visceral but devoid of melodrama.

cues.delivery: Measured observation. Jab is thinking through the impossible; pace should be deliberate.
cues.from: The four hounds stood in the road and did not come, and Jab stood in four feet of dead grass and let himself, for about five seconds, actually think.
cues.through: They had not come at him.
cues.reason: Establishes the internal realization that drives the tactical shift.

cues.delivery: Jab's voice is flat and detached. The realization that light acts as a fence must feel like a cold calculation.
cues.from: "Huh," said Jab, out loud, in a voice that did not sound like a frightened person.
cues.through: It was not a weapon to them. It had never once been a weapon to them. It was a fence, and he had spent the last four hundred paces carrying a fence around in his fist and waving it at things and wondering why they would not come and be cut.
cues.reason: Captures the shift from fear to tactical understanding.

cues.delivery: Command is low-register and urgent. Jab speaks as a partner to Tonk.
cues.through: It came all at once, the way the stillness had come: one moment four animals standing side-on in a road and the next moment four animals moving, and every one of them came at the south side.
cues.reason: Sets the stakes for the incoming attack.

cues.delivery: Rhythmic and immediate. The fight is clumsy and desperate; Jab's movements are reactive.
cues.through: "You heard him!" roared the voice. "Lights right! Everything lit goes RIGHT!"
cues.reason: The combat sequence requires a visceral, non-choreographed cadence.

cues.delivery: Toren speaks conversationally despite the violence. The contrast highlights his unnatural strength.
cues.from: "No," said the big boy, in a completely conversational voice, as if a door had blown open.
cues.reason: Character differentiation through rhythm and tone.

cues.delivery: Dessa's voice is flat and hard. The threat from the pipe must feel like a physical law.
cues.from: "Two," said a girl's voice, flat and hard, from up on the bank behind them. "Two left. One's in the ditch on the east, about fifteen feet down, not moving, and I don't like it."
cues.through: She put herself across the mouth of the pipe with her boots in the water and her blade lit and lying flat along the stone, and the thing in the culvert came out into a grey light and did not get one whole body-length out of the arch.
cues.reason: Maintains clinical detachment during the final combat beat.

cues.delivery: Jab's voice is broken and desperate. The attempt to wake Tonk requires physical exhaustion.
cues.from: "No," he said. "No, no, no — Tonk. Tonk. Look at me."
cues.through: He had learned that much in sixteen days and it had cost him an hour of a bad night and the use of his hands. Don't ask it when you want an answer. He could not stop wanting. There was no world in which he was going to stop wanting. But he could stop asking — he could let go of the reaching part, the leaning-on-a-door part, the whole miserable business of trying to make a river run uphill — and he did, and he sat there in the ash with his hand on his brother's chest and did nothing at all.
cues.reason: Captures the emotional core of Jab's fear for his brother.

cues.delivery: The transfer is physical and warm. Jab's voice should be quiet as the energy leaves him.
cues.from: And it went out of him without asking his permission.
cues.through: Then the thing in his chest went out like a lamp, and he found he was sitting down.
cues.reason: Avoids magical spectacle; focuses on the cost of the act.

cues.delivery: Dessa is observational and direct. Jab's responses are exhausted but clear.
cues.from: "You went down on your left knee there," she said. "And then you got up and went right, and then you fell over your own frame."
cues.through: "Then you'll walk beside him," she said, "and you'll hold his hand, and that's the same thing and it weighs less." She put two fingers in her mouth and whistled up the road, and it was the loudest noise anybody had made all night. "Otto! Bring the barrow!"
cues.reason: Returns to the narrator's grounded stance after the emotional climax.

pauses.after: It was the strangest five seconds of his life. His left sleeve was filling up. His brother was making a noise behind his heels that he could not afford to listen to. There were things standing eighteen feet away that had come apart into ash under his hands and would do the same to a four-year-old in a quarter of the time, and all of that was true and none of it was the point, and the point was this:
pauses.reason: Completed thought on Jab's internal state before the realization.
Emphasis on the critical realization that follows.

pauses.after: It was not a weapon to them. It had never once been a weapon to them. It was a fence, and he had spent the last four hundred paces carrying a fence around in his fist and waving it at things and wondering why they would not come and be cut.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and paragraph turn after Jab's realization of the fence mechanic.

pauses.before: They come at me! They come at the dark bit — put your light on where you don't want them!
pauses.reason: Emphasis on 'dark' to clarify the tactical instruction.

pauses.after: "You heard him!" roared the voice. "Lights right! Everything lit goes RIGHT!"
pauses.reason: Pause for the tactical shift as allies take over the fight.

pauses.after: She put herself across the mouth of the pipe with her boots in the water and her blade lit and lying flat along the stone, and the thing in the culvert came out into a grey light and did not get one whole body-length out of the arch.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing; silence after the combat ends and before the medical crisis begins.

pauses.before: because his brother had stopped making any noise at all.
pauses.reason: Emphasis on the silence that signals collapse.

pauses.after: Jab had seen this. He had seen it in a snow shelter fourteen nights ago by firelight with four warm stones at his brother's back.
pauses.reason: Continuation of Jab's recognition of Tonk's condition.

pauses.after: He had learned that much in sixteen days and it had cost him an hour of a bad night and the use of his hands. Don't ask it when you want an answer. He could not stop wanting. There was no world in which he was going to stop wanting. But he could stop asking — he could let go of the reaching part, the leaning-on-a-door part, the whole miserable business of trying to make a river run uphill — and he did, and he sat there in the ash with his hand on his brother's chest and did nothing at all.
pauses.reason: Pause for the physical sensation of the warmth leaving Jab; a moment of exhaustion.

pauses.reason: Isolates 'letting go' as the pivotal action for healing.

pauses.before: They went right because of the light,
pauses.reason: Emphasis on 'light' to confirm Jab's discovery.
Completed thought on Jab's realization about his own tactical error.
